_comment: Rock with no water in it: no aquifers, no wet pockets, no perched pools, and no springs running out of
the cave walls. The rock's own water table is switched dry (Carvers.DRY), which is also what the
hollows an underground cuts answer to, so `dry rock` dries a great hall as well as a cave. A cave
under a sea still meets the sea, and the lava at the bottom of the world stays.
It refuses wet rock as well as drying what is left, so `dry flooded rock` is two words that cannot
both hold and is charged as the contradiction it is -- flooded rock has no dry to be set, and would
otherwise simply have won. Laid on the whole Age it also offers a drier air, which yields to anything
that says more about the climate.
